roles.EN: entity — JOIN keys (PKs, surrogate keys, FK integrity, compound grain, type stability)
roles.DM: dimension — GROUP BY axes (accepted values, cardinality, mutual exclusivity, conformance)
roles.MS: measure — aggregated facts (range, additivity, currency, distribution, NaN/Inf)
roles.TM: time — date/datetime columns; carries a sub-role segment
roles.MD: model — cross-column / model-level concerns (grain, contract, versioning, parity)

dama_dimensions.Completeness: The proportion of stored data against the potential of 100% — required values are present.
dama_dimensions.Uniqueness: No entity instance is recorded more than once; nothing is duplicated against how it is identified.
dama_dimensions.Timeliness: The degree to which data represents reality at the required point in time — it is current enough.
dama_dimensions.Validity: Data conforms to the syntax (format, type, range) of its definition — values are in the allowed domain.
dama_dimensions.Accuracy: The degree to which data correctly describes the real-world object or event it models.
dama_dimensions.Consistency: The absence of difference when comparing representations of a thing across datasets / over time.

wang_strong._about: The genuine Wang & Strong (1996) 'Beyond Accuracy' framework — 15 dimensions in 4 categories — used here as the SECONDARY, consumer-perception cross-reference. (This name was previously misapplied to the DAMA-UK6 values, now correctly under `dama_dimensions`.)

_crosswalk._about: The documented default mapping from a rule's DAMA-UK6 dimension to its Wang-Strong dimension. Per-rule `wang_strong` arrays start from this image and are enriched where a representational/interpretability dimension distinctly applies.

detection_modes.deterministic: The trigger (applies_when) is statically determinable AND the required artifact is statically detectable from manifest.json / schema yml / SQL. `adaf check taxonomy` gates it fully (pass/fail) with no LLM.
detection_modes.hybrid: The artifact's PRESENCE/ABSENCE is statically detectable, but whether the rule APPLIES (or whether the artifact is adequate) needs judgement. `adaf check` flags a missing artifact where the precondition is detectable; `adaf review` judges applicability/adequacy.
detection_modes.llm: Neither applicability nor adequacy has a reliable static signal (semantic intent, refactor intent, anomaly-monitoring value). Only `adaf review` evaluates it.

rules.title: Assert single-column uniqueness and non-null
rules.summary: unique + not_null together on a single-column grain key.
rules.applies_when: Column is the single-column grain (PK/surrogate) of a dim/fact, or a JOIN key downstream.

rules.title: Assert a composite grain is unique
rules.summary: unique_combination_of_columns over the tuple that defines one row.
rules.applies_when: Grain spans 2+ columns (e.g. order_id + line_number).

rules.title: Enforce referential integrity on FKs
rules.summary: relationships test that every FK value exists in the parent.
rules.applies_when: Column is a foreign key used in a JOIN ON to another model.

rules.title: Scope FK integrity past soft-deletes
rules.summary: relationships_where excludes soft-deleted/cancelled parents from the FK check.
rules.applies_when: FK target has soft-deletes (deleted_at / is_active) that would false-positive a plain relationships test.

rules.title: Guard against surrogate hash collisions
rules.summary: Test the natural key's uniqueness alongside the surrogate's — unique on the hash alone hides collisions.
rules.framework_first: dbt core unique (on both surrogate and natural key)
rules.applies_when: Surrogate key is a hash (dbt_utils.generate_surrogate_key) of natural columns.

rules.title: Keep join-key data types stable across relations
rules.summary: Contract data_type on both sides of a join so an INT64↔STRING key mismatch fails at parse, not at runtime fanout.
rules.applies_when: A JOIN key crosses models that could drift in type (e.g. string id vs int id).

rules.title: Constrain a categorical to its enum
rules.summary: accepted_values enum contract on a categorical column.
rules.applies_when: Column is a low-cardinality categorical used in GROUP BY / filters (status, type, country).

rules.title: Bound a dimension's distinct-value count
rules.summary: expect_column_unique_value_count_to_be_between catches silent explosion/collapse of a category set.
rules.applies_when: A categorical's distinct count should stay within a known band (e.g. ~200 countries).

rules.title: Govern shared dimension values from one seed
rules.summary: A shared seed is the source of truth so the same dimension means the same thing across models.
rules.framework_first: dbt core relationships against a seed
rules.applies_when: The same dimension (e.g. region, channel) appears in multiple marts and must conform.

rules.title: Sibling boolean flags must not co-fire
rules.summary: expression_is_true that at most one of a set of sibling booleans is true per row.
rules.applies_when: Model has mutually-exclusive flags (is_new / is_returning) that must sum to <= 1.

rules.title: Detect per-dimension count anomalies
rules.summary: Elementary dimension anomaly test flags when a category's row share drifts from history.
rules.applies_when: A high-value categorical's distribution must be monitored over time; project already runs Elementary.

rules.title: Bound a measure to a plausible range
rules.summary: accepted_range rejects negatives / impossible magnitudes on an amount or count.
rules.applies_when: Column is a numeric measure with a known floor/ceiling (price >= 0, pct 0-100).

rules.title: Tag a measure's additivity
rules.summary: Declare additive / semi-additive / non-additive so the measure isn't summed across a forbidden dimension.
rules.applies_when: Column is aggregated (SUM/AVG) and could be wrongly summed across time/entity (e.g. a balance, a ratio).

rules.title: Amounts always travel with a currency code
rules.summary: Every monetary amount column has a non-null currency_code companion; not_null + contract.
rules.applies_when: Model has a monetary amount that could mix currencies if currency_code is missing/null.

rules.title: Trap divide-by-zero / NaN / Inf
rules.summary: expression_is_true that a ratio/rate is finite (denominator != 0, value not NaN/Inf).
rules.applies_when: Measure is a ratio/rate computed by division where the denominator can be zero.

rules.title: Detect mean/stdev distribution drift
rules.summary: Elementary anomaly test on a measure's mean/stdev vs its history.
rules.applies_when: A headline measure must be monitored for silent drift over time; project runs Elementary.

rules.title: No future dates, no sentinels
rules.summary: Event timestamp is not in the future and not a 1900-01-01 / 9999-12-31 sentinel.
rules.applies_when: Column is an event timestamp used in WHERE / arithmetic / window functions.

rules.title: Ordered timestamp pairs stay ordered
rules.summary: expression_is_true that shipped_at >= ordered_at, updated_at >= created_at, etc.
rules.applies_when: Model has two timestamps with a required ordering (start/end, created/updated).

rules.title: TIMESTAMP vs DATETIME contract
rules.summary: Contract the column's time type (TIMESTAMP=instant vs DATETIME=wall-clock) on BigQuery.
rules.applies_when: A datetime column's TZ semantics matter and could drift between TIMESTAMP and DATETIME.

rules.title: No gaps in a date spine
rules.summary: sequential_values on date_day proves the spine has no missing days.
rules.applies_when: Column is a date-grain dimension built by GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC / a date spine.

rules.title: Source freshness + model recency
rules.summary: source freshness block plus a model-level recency check on loaded_at / audit timestamp.
rules.framework_first: source freshness: block; escalate to dbt_utils.recency / elementary.freshness_anomalies
rules.applies_when: Column is loaded_at / an audit timestamp, or the model has an upstream source to monitor.

rules.title: The four SCD2 tests, together
rules.summary: valid_from/valid_to: no overlaps, no gaps, exactly one current row per key, valid_to>valid_from.
rules.applies_when: Model is a Type-2 slowly-changing dimension (snapshot with valid_from/valid_to).

rules.title: Detect freshness drift against a learned cadence
rules.summary: Elementary freshness_anomalies / event_freshness_anomaly flag when the gap since the last load (or last event) deviates from the table's learned update cadence — a moving SLA where no fixed one fits.
rules.applies_when: A loaded_at / event timestamp whose update cadence is irregular or seasonal, so a fixed source freshness: SLA (TM-AU-01) is too brittle; project runs Elementary (prod).

rules.title: Every model declares and tests its grain
rules.summary: Exactly one unique_combination_of_columns naming the model's grain. The non-negotiable baseline.
rules.applies_when: ALWAYS — every model must name and test its grain. Flag any model missing it.

rules.title: Enforce the model's shape with a contract
rules.summary: contract.enforced: true pins column names + types at parse time (shape, not content).
rules.applies_when: Model is a published/consumed mart or has downstream/external consumers.

rules.title: Ship a breaking change as v=N+1
rules.summary: dbt model versions let consumers migrate before the old version is retired.
rules.applies_when: A breaking schema change to a contracted/consumed model is being shipped.

rules.title: Prove a refactor changed nothing
rules.summary: audit_helper diff of old vs new relation proves a refactor is row-for-row identical.
rules.applies_when: PR refactors a model's SQL with the intent of zero output change.

rules.title: Unit-test branching SQL logic
rules.summary: dbt 1.8 unit tests assert fixed input rows produce expected output for CASE/window logic.
rules.applies_when: Model has non-trivial branching logic (CASE, window, dedup) whose correctness isn't a data test.

rules.title: Bound a model's row count
rules.summary: expect_table_row_count_to_be_between catches a model that silently emptied or exploded.
rules.applies_when: Model's row count should sit in a stable band (e.g. a daily mart).

rules.title: Detect row-volume anomalies over time
rules.summary: Elementary volume anomaly test flags row-count drift vs history (smarter than a fixed band).
rules.applies_when: Model's volume must be monitored over time and a fixed band is too brittle; project runs Elementary.

rules.title: Detect schema drift on sources you don't own
rules.summary: Elementary schema_changes / schema_changes_from_baseline flag added/removed/retyped columns on a source a parse-time contract can't guard.
rules.applies_when: Model reads an upstream source/table you don't control, so a dbt contract can't catch the drift at parse time; project runs Elementary (prod).

rules.title: Automated table-wide column monitors
rules.summary: Elementary all_columns_anomalies / column_anomalies watch null %, min/max/avg, zero-count and string length across columns as a safety net beyond hand-written per-column rules.
rules.applies_when: A wide model where hand-coding a rule per column is impractical and you want automated drift coverage on column statistics; project runs Elementary (prod).

rules.title: Validate a JSON column against an expected shape
rules.summary: Elementary json_schema asserts a semi-structured/JSON column conforms to a declared shape — the keys and types a parse-time contract can't see inside.
rules.applies_when: Model publishes/consumes a JSON (or stringified-JSON) column whose internal keys/types must hold and can't be pinned by a column data_type contract.
